title: Children are always protected during wars and conflicts because there are laws and organisations to help them.
body: Even though laws and organisations aim to protect children, conflict can still put them in danger. Many lose homes, schools or family, and may not get the help they need. Protection efforts are vital, but they can't always reach every child in time.

body: Migration is when people move between places and across borders. Some migrants need support when living in a new place.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: All migrants need the basics, like shelter, but other kinds of support can depend on why they moved.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Refugees and asylum seekers have rights under international law and are helped by government, charities and communities.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Even migrants who choose to move still need support, for example, social support, language or schooling and work advice.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Supporting migrants allows them to share their skills and get involved in society.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Only asylum seekers need support when they move to a new country.
body: All migrants may need support. Refugees often flee danger and need urgent help, but even those who move for work, study or family benefit from language classes, job advice and community events to settle in and feel part of their new home.

body: Immigration is when people move to a country to live there. Emigration is when people move out of a country.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Immigration control refers to the ways countries manage and limit who can enter, stay or settle.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Immigration control is beneficial for planning, safety and services.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Its drawbacks include long delays, labour shortages and the risk of treating people unfairly.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Decisions about immigration involve complex matters, and it is likely that the debate will continue for some time.

title: immigration

title: Immigration control means stopping all immigration.
body: Immigration control does not mean stopping all immigration. It means managing who can come, when and why, using systems like visas, border checks and rules. The aim is to make immigration fair, safe and planned, not to block everyone from entering.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Migration affects both the communities people leave and the communities they move to.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Migrants may fill workforce gaps, start businesses and introduce new cultures, languages and ideas that enrich society.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: They may need extra support with housing, language or education, and some communities might experience tension.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Migration may bring benefits like remittances or migrants may return with skills/experience that help communities grow.
attribution_text: A citizenship lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: There are many challenges, including the loss of skilled workers and emotional strain from long-term family separation.
